name: Fallingwater
unique: Frank Lloyd Wright's house cantilevered over a waterfall, with the stream running through the living room and the furniture built into the architecture.
buzz: The guided tour is excellent and strictly timed; photography inside is banned. Book weeks ahead in fall.

name: Ricketts Glen Falls Trail
customer: Hikers, photographers, families with older kids
unique: Twenty two named waterfalls in a single seven-mile loop down and back up a hemlock gorge, the highest concentration of falls on one trail in the East.
buzz: Hikers call it the best waterfall hike in Pennsylvania and warn the rocks are slick; the falls trail closes in ice.

name: Barnes Foundation
unique: Dr. Barnes collected 181 Renoirs, 69 Cezannes and 59 Matisses and hung them in ensembles meant to teach visual thinking, now in a Tod Williams building on the Parkway.
buzz: The hang is the lesson and people either love or fight it; book a timed ticket and give it three hours, the collection is denser than it looks.

name: Eastern State Penitentiary
dates: Year round; Halloween haunt in fall
unique: The world's first true penitentiary, now a stabilized ruin where Al Capone's cell is restored and the corridors still carry the acoustic isolation the Quakers designed.
buzz: The audio tour narrated by Steve Buscemi is a highlight; Terror Behind the Walls is one of the best haunts in the country.

name: Knoebels Amusement Resort
unique: A free admission park in the woods with three wood coasters, a 1913 carousel, a coal fired steam train and pierogies, all priced by the ride.
buzz: Enthusiasts rank Phoenix among the best wooden coasters in the world; families like that parking and admission are free and food is cheap.

name: Mahoning Drive-In Theater
unique: A 1949 drive in that refuses to go digital, projecting only 35mm prints on a huge screen, with a volunteer crew and a crowd that brings lawn chairs and cheers the reel changes.
buzz: Film people drive hours for it and the atmosphere is a party. Bring bug spray, cash for the snack bar and a radio for the sound.

name: Longwood Gardens
unique: A du Pont estate of 1,100 acres with a conservatory the size of a cathedral, an organ with 10,000 pipes, and fountain shows after dark.
buzz: Winter is the secret season for the conservatory; summer fountain shows are crowded but worth staying for.

name: Andy Warhol Museum
unique: Seven floors holding 900 paintings, the Silver Clouds room and Warhol's time capsules, in the industrial building on the North Shore where he was born a few miles away.
buzz: The top floor films and the cloud room are the ones people remember; the permanent collection is so deep that a second visit is different.

name: Flight 93 National Memorial
unique: A field in Somerset County where the fourth hijacked plane came down, marked by a white marble wall that follows the flight path and a tower of wind chimes with a bell for each passenger.
buzz: The walk from the visitor center to the wall is a quarter mile and the sound of the wind chimes is what people describe; it is quiet and free.

name: Gettysburg Battlefield
unique: Twenty five square miles of preserved battle line, Little Round Top, the Wheatfield, Pickett's Charge, best seen by bike or with a licensed guide in your car.
buzz: Licensed guides are worth every dollar; the auto tour alone misses the story. The cyclorama is dated but moving.

name: Little League World Series
unique: The world championship for 12 year olds, played on a hillside field where fans sit on the grass and teams from Japan, Venezuela and Texas stay in the same village.
buzz: Admission is free and the hill fills early; locals say the international teams and the Lamade Stadium atmosphere beat most professional games.

name: Ohiopyle Whitewater
unique: The Lower Yough packs Class III–IV rapids into a gorge with natural waterslides and swimming holes, an hour from Fallingwater.
buzz: Outfitters are praised for safety and river knowledge; the guided Lower Yough is the right first trip. Water is cold even in August.

name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
unique: A public access glass studio in a converted warehouse with classes in blowing, flameworking and casting, plus free gallery shows by resident artists.
buzz: The teaching is patient and the facility is serious; weekend intro classes are the gateway.

name: Reading Terminal Market
unique: An 1893 train shed turned food hall: Amish butchers, a century old pretzel bakery, a Pennsylvania Dutch diner and the best cheesesteak argument in the city.
buzz: Go hungry and wander; DiNic's roast pork is the local pick over the cheesesteak. Seating is a blood sport at noon.

name: Delaware Water Gap
unique: The river cuts through the Kittatinny Ridge at a notch you can climb above on the Appalachian Trail, with a beach, a canoe launch and a view of New Jersey from the top.
buzz: The Mount Tammany red dot trail is steep and crowded and the reward is the gap from above; the river beach is the easy alternative.

name: Duquesne Incline
company: Society for the Preservation of the Duquesne Heights Incline
unique: A wooden 1877 funicular up Mount Washington, still run by hand by a operator in the upper station, ending at the three rivers view that defines the city.
buzz: Ride up at dusk and walk down the steps or take it back; the upper station has a small museum of the machinery and the fare is cash friendly.

name: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
unique: The ridge where the modern raptor count began, with a lookout over the Kittatinny where hundreds of hawks and eagles pass on a good September day.
buzz: Volunteers with clickers will teach you to identify a bird on the wing; the North Lookout is a short steep walk and the trail system continues for miles.

name: Hersheypark
unique: A chocolate company's employee picnic ground turned 121 acre park with 15 coasters, a water park and a zoo, ringed by the smell of cocoa from the factory.
buzz: Candymonium and Skyrush are the coaster draws; buy tickets online, arrive at opening and use the preview night if you are staying over.

name: Kinzua Bridge Skywalk
unique: A 301 foot tall railroad viaduct that a tornado tore down in 2003, now a glass floored observation deck at the edge of the wreckage with the twisted towers still standing in the valley.
buzz: The glass floor is the thrill and the fallen towers are the photo; the walk out is 600 feet and the valley is best in fall.

name: Mercer Museum
customer: Tool people, history fans, architecture students
unique: A concrete castle built to hold one man's collection of pre-industrial American tools, with a whaleboat hanging from the ceiling and a walkway that spirals up through six floors.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and people describe it as a cathedral of hand tools; allow two hours because every case has something strange.

name: Mutter Museum
customer: Medical people, teens, the morbidly curious
unique: A Victorian cabinet of medical oddities: the Hyrtl skull collection, wax casts of disease, Einstein's brain slices and a giant colon named after its owner.
buzz: People either find it fascinating or leave early; reviewers praise the respectful framing of human remains. Not for young kids.

name: Presque Isle State Park
company: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
unique: A seven mile sand spit curving into Lake Erie with eleven beaches, a flat multi use trail and a lagoon where migrating birds pile up in spring.
buzz: Sunsets over the bay side are the local ritual; the peninsula trail is flat and the beaches get crowded only in July.

name: SteelStacks
unique: The Bethlehem Steel plant turned arts campus, where the blast furnaces stand lit at night above a lawn that hosts free summer concerts and a film series.
buzz: The furnaces at night are the photograph everyone takes; the free Levitt Pavilion shows are the local summer ritual.

name: Touchstone Center for Crafts
unique: A craft campus in the Laurel Highlands with blacksmithing, glass, ceramics and wood workshops, plus lodging in cabins on the grounds.
buzz: The classes are affordable and the setting is woodsy; it is close to Ohiopyle and Fallingwater for a combined trip.

name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
unique: The winter camp where Washington's army survived 1777 with a reconstructed log city, earthworks you can walk and a 3,500 acre park with a bike trail through it.
buzz: The ranger talks and the Muhlenberg Brigade huts are the best part; the loop road is flat and the park is free, which surprises people.

name: Brandywine River Museum
unique: A converted gristmill on the Brandywine holding three generations of Wyeth paintings, including the Olson House canvases and N.C. Wyeth's illustrations.
buzz: The top floor galleries with the Andrew Wyeth rooms are the reason to come; the mill windows look out on the river he painted.

name: Bushkill Falls
unique: Eight waterfalls on a privately owned gorge with boardwalks and stairs, the tallest dropping 100 feet, reached by a mile of trail in the Poconos.
buzz: The red trail covers everything and takes two hours; it is a paid attraction, which people either resent or appreciate for the upkeep.

name: Harley-Davidson York Factory Tour
customer: Motorcycle people, engineers, families with teens
unique: The plant where every Harley frame and fuel tank is made and painted, walked on a catwalk above the assembly line with closed toe shoes required.
buzz: Riders call it a pilgrimage and non riders are surprised by the robots; tours fill weeks out and the plant shuts in some holiday weeks.

name: Horseshoe Curve
unique: A 1.8 mile curve engineered in 1854 to lift the Pennsylvania Railroad over the Alleghenies, with a funicular up to a viewing park where 100 car freight trains still grind past.
buzz: Check the train schedule at the visitor center and time your visit; the funicular and the view of the curve from above are the whole experience.

name: Jim Thorpe
unique: A Victorian era coal town in a gorge, with a stone main street, a 1883 opera house and the grave of the athlete it renamed itself for.
buzz: The architecture and the setting between two mountains are the reasons to walk it and the Lehigh Gorge bike trail starts here; the town is busy in fall.

name: Pennsylvania Grand Canyon
unique: A 47 mile gorge of Pine Creek with two rim overlooks, a rail trail at the bottom and 800 foot rock walls that turn orange in October.
buzz: The west rim overlooks are the easy view and the Turkey Path is the steep way down; the canyon is at its best in the first week of October.

name: Steamtown National Historic Site
unique: A working rail yard in the old Lackawanna shops with a roundhouse, a turntable you can watch turn a locomotive and short steam excursions through the valley.
buzz: Train people spend all day and families do the roundhouse and the short ride; check the excursion schedule before going.

name: Field of Screams
customer: Haunted house fans, teens, young adults
unique: Four attractions on a farm, including a haunted hayride through the woods, a den of darkness and a corn maze, run with a level of set design that has kept it nationally ranked.
buzz: The hayride is the signature and the actors are relentless; go with a group and buy the combo pass. Lines peak after dark.

name: Pennhurst Asylum
unique: A haunted attraction inside a real abandoned institution for people with disabilities, with tunnels, wards and a history that is darker than any actor in makeup.
buzz: The setting does most of the work and the history is worth reading before you go; some visitors find the spectacle uncomfortable given the real suffering.
customer: Haunted house fans, teens, young adults

name: Eisenhower National Historic Site
unique: The farm Eisenhower bought as a weekend retreat that became the White House in the summer, with the Angus cattle, the putting green and the house as he left it.
buzz: The house and the farm are the tour and the shuttle from the battlefield visitor center is the only way in; history people say it is the human side of the general.

name: Erie Maritime Museum
unique: The home port of the Brig Niagara, Perry's reconstructed flagship from the Battle of Lake Erie, with a museum on the 1813 battle and a winter shipyard you can watch.
buzz: Sailing on the Niagara is the splurge and books out; the museum alone explains why a freshwater lake had a naval war.

name: Fonthill Castle
unique: Henry Mercer's concrete house with 44 rooms, 32 stairwells and a ceiling of Moravian tiles, built by hand with no architect and no plan.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and the stairs are steep; visitors say it feels like a medieval house built by a obsessive.

name: Johnstown Flood Museum
unique: The 1889 flood that killed 2,200 people when a private dam gave way, told in the old Carnegie library with a relief map, survivor accounts and an Oscar winning film.
buzz: The film runs on a loop and still lands; visitors say the scale of the disaster is hard to hold until you see the map of the valley.

name: Kennywood
unique: A trolley park from 1898 with three wooden coasters, a 1920s Noah's Ark walkthrough and the Thunderbolt, all on a bluff above the Monongahela.
buzz: Coaster people rank the Phantom's Revenge and the Jack Rabbit; the park is small enough that a day pass covers everything twice.

name: Lackawanna Coal Mine Tour
unique: A mine car drops you 300 feet into a anthracite seam where a former miner explains the work at a temperature of 53 degrees year round.
buzz: The guides are retired miners and the stories are the tour; bring a jacket and expect to duck, the seam is low.

name: Lancaster Central Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating farmers market in the country, in a brick hall where Amish farm stands sell scrapple, chow chow and whoopie pies beside Lebanese and Jamaican counters.
buzz: Saturday is the crush and Tuesday is the locals; the smoked meats and the pretzels are the standing orders and cash is still normal.

name: Pennsylvania State Capitol
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A Beaux Arts capitol Roosevelt called the handsomest in the nation, with a 272 foot dome, Moravian tiles and a limestone staircase modeled on the Paris opera.
buzz: The free tour is the only way into the rotunda and the House chamber; the tile work is what visitors photograph.

name: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
customer: Mosaic people, photographers, South Street wanderers
unique: Half a block of South Street tiled by Isaiah Zagar with bottles, mirrors, bicycle wheels and folk art, with a basement grotto you crawl through.
buzz: People come for a photo and stay for the story of the neighborhood; the outdoor lot needs a ticket and the surrounding alleys are free.

name: Phipps Conservatory
unique: A Victorian glasshouse in Schenley Park with a tropical forest under glass, a butterfly room and a Center for Sustainable Landscapes that is one of the greenest buildings in the world.
buzz: The winter flower show is the local tradition and the summer butterfly room is the family draw; the glasshouse is hot in July.

name: Strasburg Rail Road
unique: The oldest short line railroad in the country, running a steam locomotive 45 minutes through Amish farm fields from a 1830s depot.
buzz: Book the open air car and sit on the left; children want the steam engine and the shop sells the wooden version for the ride home.

name: Yuengling Brewery Tour
unique: America's oldest brewery, dug into a hillside where the cellars are 150 feet of hand cut sandstone and the tour ends with samples in a 19th century bottling house.
buzz: The cave cellars are the part people remember; tours are free but fill early and the tasting is short.

name: Appalachian Trail Museum
unique: The only museum devoted to the Appalachian Trail, in an 1820s ironmaster's mansion where thru hikers still stop for a bunk, with packs, boots and journals from the trail.
buzz: Thru hikers sign the register and volunteers feed them; in June the porch is full of people who walked from Georgia.

name: Berkey Creamery
unique: The university dairy that makes ice cream from its own herd and sells it in a plant on campus, with a viewing window over the production floor.
buzz: The lines run out the door on football weekends and the Peachy Paterno was renamed; the half gallon is the move if you are driving.

name: Bloomsburg Fair
unique: The largest agricultural fair in the state, nine days of draft horse pulls, a mile of food stands and a grandstand concert series in a town of 15,000.
buzz: Locals take the week off; the livestock barns and the harness racing are the real fair and the midway is the noise around it.

name: Bucks County Playhouse
unique: A summer stock theater in a 1790s mill on the Delaware, where Broadway tryouts and well known actors have worked since 1939.
buzz: The building and the river setting are half the experience and the productions are professional; the town is walkable before the show.

name: National Civil War Museum
unique: A hilltop museum that tells the war from both sides with a balance rare among Civil War sites, from the 1850s causes through reconstruction, with a large collection of soldiers' letters.
buzz: Visitors say it is the honest overview the battlefields do not give; the walk up the hill is steep and the view over Harrisburg is the bonus.

name: National Museum of Industrial History
unique: A Smithsonian affiliate in a former Bethlehem Steel building, with a working steam engine, the only remaining screw propeller from the Titanic's sister ship and a silk loom you can run.
buzz: The volunteers start the engines and talk forever; the machine shop is the best part and children can operate several exhibits.

name: Penn's Cave
unique: The only all water cave tour in the country, a flat bottom boat through a limestone passage under a mountain and out the other side, with a wildlife park above.
buzz: The boat is the whole tour and children love it; the cave is 52 degrees and the wildlife park is a separate walk.

name: Pine Creek Rail Trail
unique: A 62 mile crushed stone trail down the floor of the Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania along Pine Creek, with shuttle services that drop you at the top.
buzz: The down hill run from Ansonia to Jersey Shore is the standard half day; the shuttle books out in fall and the trail is flat enough for hybrids.

name: Pocono Raceway
unique: A triangle shaped superspeedway where you can camp inside the infield, watch three turns at once and see the cars come at you down the long front stretch.
buzz: The infield camping is the experience and the traffic afterwards is the warning; the July race is the big one.

name: Polymath Park
unique: A hillside with three Frank Lloyd Wright houses, two of them moved here from elsewhere, that you can tour and then sleep in.
buzz: Wright people call it the only place to stay overnight in a Wright house in the east; tours need booking and the houses are small.

name: US Army Heritage and Education Center
unique: A free army museum with a mile long outdoor trail of reproduced fortifications from the French and Indian War to Vietnam, plus a research library of soldiers' letters.
buzz: The outdoor heritage trail is the surprise and you can walk inside a bunker and a trench; the indoor galleries are small and rotate.

name: Bryn Athyn Cathedral
company: General Church of the New Jerusalem
customer: Architecture people, stained glass fans, quiet seekers
unique: A Gothic cathedral built by hand in the 1910s by craftsmen who worked without straight lines, with glass made on the grounds and a hilltop view over the Pennypack valley.
buzz: Architects call the craftsmanship a century ahead of its time; the cathedral is free and the neighboring Glencairn Museum is the paid tour.

name: Idlewild Park
unique: A 1878 trolley park in the Laurel Highlands with Storybook Forest, a 1930s walk through nursery rhymes, and a wooden coaster in the woods.
buzz: Parents say Storybook Forest is the reason to come before children turn eight; the water park and the coaster extend the day.

name: Italian Market
unique: Nine blocks of 9th Street where cheesemakers, butchers and tortilla factories still work behind open counters, with the Philadelphia side of the market running since the 1880s.
buzz: Go on a weekday morning and start at the top; the weekend crowd is a wall and the produce prices are the best in the city.

name: Johnstown Inclined Plane
unique: The steepest vehicular inclined plane in the world at 70 percent grade, built as an escape route after the flood and still carrying cars and people up the hill.
buzz: The ride is short and the view from the top over the Conemaugh valley is the point; the operator will explain the counterweight.

name: Palmer Museum of Art
unique: A university art museum with American painting, Japanese prints and a sculpture garden, free on the Penn State campus.
buzz: The collection is broader than expected and it is free; the new building is a short walk from the student union.

name: Pioneer Tunnel Coal Mine
unique: A narrow gauge mine train that carries you 1,800 feet into a working anthracite vein, then a steam locomotive ride on the surface along the old colliery.
buzz: The guides are former miners and the mine is cold; children like the train and adults like the stories about breaker boys.

name: Railroaders Memorial Museum
customer: Train people, families, labor history fans
unique: The old PRR master mechanics building holding a K4 steam locomotive, a cab you can climb into and the story of the Altoona shops that built and repaired the railroad.
buzz: The simulator and the cab are for children and the labor history galleries are for adults; combine it with Horseshoe Curve on one ticket.

name: Roadside America
customer: Families, road trippers, model train fans
unique: A 6,000 square foot miniature village of tiny houses, farms and a working railroad, built by one man over decades and lit by a day to night show.
buzz: It is a time capsule of a roadside attraction and children are hypnotized; the night show is kitsch perfection.

name: Seven Tubs Nature Area
unique: A creek that has drilled a series of round pools into the bedrock at the foot of a mountain, with a trail through the glen.
buzz: The tubs are the photograph and the trail is short and steep; it is free and cool in summer and the water is dangerous after rain.

name: Waldameer Park
unique: A trolley era park with a 1908 carousel, a wooden coaster and a water park, free to enter so you can walk the midway without buying a ride wristband.
buzz: Locals love that admission is free and parking is cheap; the Ravine Flyer II is the coaster enthusiasts come for.

name: Zippo/Case Museum
unique: The factory museum where the lighter that became a soldier's talisman is displayed with the case knives, including the prototypes and the lifetime guarantee repair bench.
buzz: Collectors come from overseas and the staff still repair any Zippo for free; the museum is free and takes an hour.

name: America on Wheels Museum
customer: Car and truck people, families, dads
unique: A transportation museum on the Lehigh River with a Mack truck gallery, a 1950s gas station and a rotating exhibit of cars you can walk around and under.
buzz: The truck room is what makes it different from every car museum; it is small and the admission is cheap enough for a rainy hour.

name: Amish Farm and House
customer: Families, first time visitors, school groups
unique: A 1805 farmhouse and working farm where a guide explains Amish schooling, barn raising and plain dress, with a bus tour into the back roads.
buzz: The house tour is better than the bus for understanding the religion; visitors say the guides answer the awkward questions honestly.

name: Baker Mansion
customer: House tour people, railroad history fans, families
unique: A Greek revival mansion built by the ironmaster who supplied the railroad, with period rooms and a collection on the Horseshoe Curve.
buzz: The house and the railroad family story are the tour; the volunteers connect it to the curve and the shops.

name: Broad Street Market
unique: Two brick market houses from the Civil War era, one of the oldest continuously operating markets in the country, with Pennsylvania Dutch stands and a growing row of Syrian and Vietnamese counters.
buzz: The stone building is the food hall and the brick building is the produce; go hungry and expect a line at the sandwich stands.

name: Centralia
unique: A town mostly erased by an underground coal fire that has burned since 1962, with a few streets, a cemetery and graffiti on the closed highway, watched over by a handful of residents.
buzz: It is eerie and quiet and you should stay on the road; the fire is still burning and the ground is unstable. A sobering detour, not a playground.

name: Dorney Park
unique: A 1884 trolley park with a 1920s carousel, a steel hypercoaster and a water park on the same ticket, in the hills above Allentown.
buzz: The water park is the summer value and the coasters are the reason enthusiasts come; weekdays in June are empty enough to loop everything.

name: Eldred World War II Museum
unique: A volunteer museum in a small town with a room for each theater of the war, mannequins in original uniforms and a collection of home front ration books and letters.
buzz: Visitors say the personal donations make it better than the big museums; it is free will donation and the volunteers are often veterans.

name: Historic Yellow Springs
unique: A former revolutionary war hospital and spa village with stone buildings, an art school and a trail along the creek.
buzz: The village is quiet and the art school studios are open to walk through; the history goes back to Washington's army.

name: Laurel Hill State Park
unique: A CCC built lake and beach in the Laurel Highlands with a hemlock gorge trail and a spillway that freezes into ice climbs in winter.
buzz: The beach is the summer draw and the gorge trail is the walk; the ice climbing at the spillway is a local winter secret.

name: Prince Gallitzin State Park
unique: A 1,600 acre lake in the Allegheny plateau with a beach, a marina and one of the largest campgrounds in the state.
buzz: The lake is the summer draw and the campground is the base; the park is quiet in the shoulder seasons.

name: Punxsutawney Groundhog Day
unique: A town of 6,000 hosts tens of thousands at 3am on a frozen hill to watch a groundhog named Phil be consulted about spring by men in top hats.
buzz: People describe it as the most American thing they've ever done; the cold is brutal and the actual prognostication lasts seconds.

name: Reading Pagoda
unique: A seven story Japanese pagoda built on a Pennsylvania mountain in 1908 by a manufacturer who never saw Japan, now a landmark above the city with a view of five counties.
buzz: It is a free oddity with a real view; the tower interior is closed most of the time and the hillside garden is where people sit.

name: Ridley Creek State Park
unique: A 2,600 acre park with a paved trail along Ridley Creek and a stone mansion, in the suburbs west of Philadelphia.
buzz: The paved trail is the easy ride and the creek is good for children; it is quiet on weekdays and busy on summer weekends.

name: York Central Market
unique: A two story brick market house with a balcony of lunch counters, where York's German farm stands became Pennsylvania Dutch lunch stands over 130 years.
buzz: The pretzel and the chicken corn soup are the orders; it is smaller than Lancaster's and easier to actually shop.

name: Crayola Experience
unique: The crayon factory's visitor center where children name and wrap their own crayon, mold wax and watch how a crayon is made, in the town where Crayola began.
buzz: Parents say three hours is the limit and the meltdown happens at the gift shop; buy tickets online and go at opening.

name: Cumberland Valley Rail Trail
unique: A crushed stone trail on the old Cumberland Valley Railroad line, running through farmland between Shippensburg and Carlisle.
buzz: The trail is flat and the farmland is the scenery; it connects to Shippensburg and the college and is quiet on weekdays.

name: French Azilum
unique: A planned refuge for French aristocrats fleeing the revolution, built in the Pennsylvania wilderness in 1793, with the foundation of the house meant for Marie Antoinette.
buzz: The story is better than the remains and the volunteer guides tell it well; it is a quiet stop on a back road along the Susquehanna.

name: Hershey's Chocolate World
unique: A free visitor center with a singing animatronic ride through the chocolate making process, a factory viewing line and a create your own chocolate bar counter.
buzz: The ride is free and dated in a way people love; the lines for the custom bar are long and the parking is paid.

name: Houdini Museum
customer: Magic fans, families, curious road trippers
unique: A magic museum and theater in a Scranton house where a working magician gives a tour of Houdini's handcuffs and escape trunks, then performs a show.
buzz: It is part museum and part vaudeville and children are the right audience; the tour and show run as one ticket.

name: Millionaires' Row
unique: A street of lumber baron mansions from the 1880s and 1890s, some 40 rooms with ballrooms and Tiffany windows, when Williamsport was the lumber capital of the world.
buzz: The self guided walking tour brochure is at the visitor center; several houses are now law offices and one is a museum.

name: Punxsutawney Weather Discovery Center
unique: A weather museum in the old post office of the town that made Groundhog Day famous, with a walk through a cloud and exhibits on forecasting.
buzz: Children like the hands on weather exhibits and the groundhog story is the local context; it is small and pairs with the town's groundhog statues.
